source: counter strike but without gravity. the map is 3D with parts that go up and down in xyz coordinate space, not just 2D or 2D with elevation changes. everything else is the same as CS. start with making everything simple polygon. don't worry about backends or multiplayer. make it first person view if possible. put enemies in random places. enemies have HP. you can shoot them and kill them. when an enemy is killed. they respawn.

answers.ask: How deep should the volume be vertically - is up and down as big as across?
answers.answer: Make the vertical depth roughly as large as the map's width and length, so it is a true cubic 3D combat space rather than a flat arena.

answers.ask: With no multiplayer and respawning bots, is there a round or a bomb at all, or is it just shooting targets?
answers.answer: It is just a simple first-person shooting target arena: no rounds, bomb, or other Counter-Strike objectives; bots respawn after being killed.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How deep should the volume be vertically - is up and down as big as across? A: Make the vertical depth roughly as large as the map's width and length, so it is a true cubic 3D combat space rather than a flat arena.
- [author] goal — Q: With no multiplayer and respawning bots, is there a round or a bomb at all, or is it just shooting targets? A: It is just a simple first-person shooting target arena: no rounds, bomb, or other Counter-Strike objectives; bots respawn after being killed.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a simple low-polygon 3D tactical shooting arena with no gravity. Make the playable volume roughly cubic, with vertical depth as large as its width and length rather than a floor with elevation changes. Distribute simple polygonal platforms, walls, and cover at varied X, Y, and Z positions so movement and firing lines extend upward, downward, and sideways through open space. Arrange multiple sightline breaks and clear gaps between structures, with no bomb sites, team objectives, or round-specific architecture. Compose the complete cubic combat volume clearly in an isometric view.

## Genre
Shooter is the dominant genre.

## Shape and preset
Use `volume-open-air`, Open Airspace, from outside Shooter's usual shape list because the arena is a true cubic zero-gravity volume with discrete surfaces rather than a ground-based lane or range. Preset: none; the target bots are mobile and randomly respawning, so neither Bomb Defusal nor the directed Aim Trainer bundle fits.

## Config requirements
Use `cover-los` for simple polygonal walls and blocks distributed throughout the cubic volume to break three-dimensional firing lines. No capture zone, team base, bomb site, building interior, weapon bench, or static target array applies after the author's answer removed those objectives.

## Layout requirements
Use `spawner-npc` for multiple enemy-bot respawn points distributed through distinct parts of the cubic volume rather than one wave mouth; choose among them at random when a bot respawns. Enemy HP, shooting, killing, respawn timing, first-person camera behavior, backend, and multiplayer are mechanics, not geometry.

## Layout components
The map is one bounded cubic open-air combat volume. Simple low-poly platforms, wall panels, and cover blocks occupy many heights and lateral positions, leaving navigable open space between them in all three axes. Cover faces several directions so no single line sees the whole volume. The outer cubic limit is the boundary; there is no privileged ground plane, flat lane network, objective site, or separate interior. Keep the full three-dimensional distribution legible in one frame.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the authoritative image must establish the cubic XYZ distribution and vertical relationships that a conventional top-down plan cannot express.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by readable individual cover pieces within a roughly equal width, length, and height. The theme is a simple low-poly tactical shooting test arena. Use `CHECK` because play occupies a true volumetric space and layered geometry may self-occlude; no P6-authored route is needed because zero-gravity movement is not constrained to a ground path.
